# Configuration

<!-- Generated by ConfigReferenceTest from the Kotlin source: edit the KDoc, then run ./gradlew updateReference. -->

Every setting of `meshLinkConfig(preset, securityProfile) { … }`. The block sets them; `build()` validates them and throws `MeshLinkException.InvalidConfig`, naming the setting, for the first one out of bounds. `MeshLinkConfig.describe()` prints each effective value with its source: `preset`, `override` or `default`.

## `meshId`

- Type: `String`
- Default: none; required

The name of the mesh: 1 to 64 bytes of UTF-8, compared byte for byte. Nodes join the same mesh only if they use the same mesh ID and security profile.

## `meshKey`

- Type: `ByteArray?`
- Default: `null`

The secret of a gated mesh: exactly 32 bytes, or `null` (the default) for an open mesh. Only nodes with the same key can link (Noise `psk3`) or recognize each other's advertisements. Not allowed with `SecurityProfile.Unsecured`. `build` copies it.

## `l2capUpgrade`

- Type: `Boolean`
- Default: `true`

Whether this node moves its links from GATT to an L2CAP connection-oriented channel where both ends can (spec "Bearer switch"); `true` by default. As peripheral it listens and offers its PSM; as central it opens a channel to a peer that offers one. Off, every link it is part of stays on GATT, which is slower but works with every peer.

## `diagnostics.debug`

- Type: `Boolean`
- Default: `false`

Whether `MeshLink.diagnostics` also emits `DiagnosticEvent.Severity.Debug` events, the detail for an investigation; `false` by default. Debug events can be frequent in a dense mesh.

## `diagnostics.platformLog`

- Type: `Boolean`
- Default: `false`

Whether each event `MeshLink.diagnostics` emits is also written to the platform log, Logcat with tag `MeshLink` on Android and `os_log` subsystem `ch.trancee.meshlink`, category `diagnostics` on iOS, whether or not the app collects them; `false` by default. On iOS only the code, name, count and numbers show publicly; `os_log` redacts every other field unless a debugger is attached or a logging profile reveals private data. On Android every field shows, so turn it on only for investigations.

## `density`

- Type: `Density`
- Default: set by the preset; see [Presets](presets.md)

How the node picks its density class (ADR 0008 decision 8); `Density.Automatic` unless pinned.

Values:

- `Density.Automatic`: The node classifies its local density from what it hears, and adapts as it changes.
- `Density.Pinned`: The node always behaves as `densityClass`. Pinning `DensityClass.Low` floods everywhere for the lowest latency, at about 2 to 4 times the load of the busiest phone (ADR 0008 decision 8).
- `DensityClass.Low`: Under about 10 peers in range: the node floods and keeps up to 6 links.
- `DensityClass.Medium`: About 10 to 50 peers in range: the node routes and keeps up to 5 links.
- `DensityClass.High`: About 50 peers in range or more: the node routes and keeps up to 5 links.

## `power`

- Type: `Power`
- Default: set by the preset; see [Presets](presets.md)

How long the node rests between scan windows in each density class.

Values:

- `Power.Balanced`: Rests 4 s at low density, 12 s at medium and 16 s at high.
- `Power.Responsive`: Rests 2.5 s at low density, 8 s at medium and 12 s at high: faster discovery for more scanning. 2.5 s, not 2 s, keeps scan starts 6.5 s apart, under Android's limit of 5 starts per 30 s.

## `routedUnicast`

- Type: `Boolean`
- Default: set by the preset; see [Presets](presets.md)

Whether `MeshLink.send` may carry a message over other nodes (ADR 0008). Off, every message is sent as `SendOptions.directOnly`: only a link to its destination carries it.

## `broadcastOrigination`

- Type: `Boolean`
- Default: set by the preset; see [Presets](presets.md)

Whether this node may originate broadcasts. Off, `MeshLink.broadcast` returns `SendResult.Rejected` with `RejectionReason.BroadcastDisabled`; the node still relays other nodes' broadcasts.

## `broadcastPriority`

- Type: `Boolean`
- Default: set by the preset; see [Presets](presets.md)

Whether this node writes broadcasts, its own and relayed, before the messages to single peers waiting on each link (ADR 0011 amendment "presets and toggles built"). A waiting message lets at most 3 broadcasts go ahead of it, so messages keep at least one write in four on a busy link. Local scheduling only: nothing is dropped and nothing changes on the wire.

## `holding`

- Type: `Boolean`
- Default: set by the preset; see [Presets](presets.md)

Whether this node holds small frames for other nodes while their destination is out of reach (spec "Holding", ADR 0014). Off, it still relays them; it never holds its own, which wait in its send queue.

## `messageLifetimeSeconds`

- Type: `Int`
- Default: set by the preset; see [Presets](presets.md)

How long a message this node sends stays deliverable: 120 to 3,600 seconds (ADR 0014 decision 2). Its expiry is the send time plus this. Until then this node retries it and relays may hold copies of it for an absent destination; after it, plus 30 s of clock skew, it is `DeliveryStatus.Expired` and every copy is dropped.

## `readReceipts.requestByDefault`

- Type: `Boolean`
- Default: set by the preset; see [Presets](presets.md)

Whether a message sent with `ReadReceiptRequest.Default` asks its recipient for a read receipt.

## `readReceipts.send`

- Type: `Boolean`
- Default: set by the preset; see [Presets](presets.md)

Whether this node sends a read receipt when the app marks a message read that asked for one. Off, the sender sees the message as unread; the node still relays other nodes' read receipts.

## `limits.maxUnicastPayload`

- Type: `Int`
- Default: set by the preset; see [Presets](presets.md)

The largest payload of a message to one peer: 4,096 to 131,072 bytes. A payload above 4,096 bytes is a large message, which travels only on a direct link or a discovered route and is never held for an absent destination.

## `limits.maxBroadcastPayload`

- Type: `Int`
- Default: set by the preset; see [Presets](presets.md)

The largest payload of a mesh broadcast: 1 to 1,024 bytes.
